evidence.quote: participants judged that maintaining a highly accommodative stance of policy was essential to foster further economic recovery and to achieve an average inflation rate of 2 percent over time.
With the economy still far from those goals, participants judged that it was likely to take some time for substantial further progress to be achieved.

Participants generally viewed the risks to the outlook for inflation as having become more balanced than was the case over most of 2020, although most still viewed the risks as weighted to the downside .

participants observed that the economy was far from achieving the Committee's broad-based and inclusive goal of maximum employment and that even with a brisk pace of improvement in the labor market, achieving this goal would take some time.
the staff to continue to judge that the risks to the baseline projection were skewed to the downside and that the uncertainty around the forecast was elevated.

parsed.rationale: The minutes strongly emphasize keeping rates at zero and continuing asset purchases for a long time, with the economy far from goals and inflation risks still weighted to the downside. An improved medium-term outlook and the dropping of the medium-term risk language only modestly temper the dovish signal.
